problem: Hannah's dialect word 'brass' ("nor no brass") is rendered as 'money', which makes Jane's pointed gloss in 29.21 ('by which I suppose you mean money') and her quotation of the word in 29.60 impossible. Keep 'brass' here so the next exchange works.
new_text: After a pause she said, "I don't understand that: you've got no house, and no brass, I suppose?"

problem: Source: "The want of house or brass (by which I suppose you mean money) does not make a beggar in your sense of the word." MODERN drops 'brass' and Jane's parenthetical gloss, losing her slightly superior, educated correction of Hannah's dialect (a character beat in the scene where she asserts she is 'book-learned').
new_text: "The lack of a house or brass (by which I suppose you mean money) does not make a beggar in the way you mean."

problem: Source has Jane quote Hannah's word back at her: "that I had no 'brass' and no house." MODERN flattens it to 'no money', losing the pointed quotation (depends on 29.20/29.21 keeping 'brass').
new_text: "But I do think badly of you," I said; "and I'll tell you why—not so much because you refused me shelter, or suspected me of being a fraud, but because you just now treated it as a kind of disgrace that I had no 'brass' and no house. Some of the best people who ever lived have been as poor as I am; and if you are a Christian, you ought not to regard poverty as a crime."

problem: Source italicises '_charity_' and then comments on it: "(I am quite sensible of the distinction drawn...)". Without the emphasis, 'the distinction you draw' has no visible referent (Jane's 'compassion' of the sisters vs St. John's 'evangelical charity' in 29.109). Restore the emphasis, as other chapters of this edition do with _..._.
new_text: "You would not like to be dependent on our hospitality for long—you would wish, I see, to move beyond my sisters' kindness and, above all, beyond my _charity_ (I am quite aware of the distinction you draw, and I do not resent it—it is fair): you want to be independent of us?"

problem: Source: "_I_ feel more inclination to put you in the way of keeping yourself" — the italic 'I' sets St. John pointedly against his sisters' 'pleasure in keeping you'. MODERN drops the emphasis, flattening the contrast. Rest of the repair is faithful.
new_text: "My sisters, you see, take pleasure in keeping you," said Mr. St. John, "as they would take pleasure in keeping and nursing a half-frozen bird that some winter wind might have blown through their window. _I_ feel more inclined to set you on the path to keeping yourself, and shall try to do so; but understand, my world is small. I am merely the minister of a poor country parish: my help must be of the humblest kind. And if you are inclined to despise the day of small things, seek more effective aid than I can offer."
